# MESA Trainings

> MESA Trainings: short, single-task tutorials for the MESA Portal at mesa.cyverse.org and its apps, written for training participants and for anyone using MESA. Each tutorial is one task in six fixed parts (what you will have, what you need, the steps, a check, the likely slip, what is next). Tutorials marked draft were written from the MESA documentation and have not been validated on the live portal. The source repository is an Open Knowledge Format (OKF v0.2) bundle: every page carries YAML frontmatter with type, provenance (generated/sources), and lifecycle (status/stale_after) fields.

Every page below is listed with three addresses that all return the same content: the rendered HTML page, its Markdown twin (page URL + `index.md`, served as text/markdown with the OKF frontmatter), and the raw source file on GitHub. Fetch whichever your tool is allowed to reach; many sandboxes permit github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com but not *.github.io.

```
Site page        https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/<path>/
Markdown twin    https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/<path>/index.md
Raw source       https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/<path>.md      (branch main; a moving target)

Content page     /tutorials/sign-in/  ->  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/sign-in.md
Section listing  /tutorials/          ->  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/index.md
```

The form https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/<path>.md also returns the same Markdown.

## Start here

- [MESA Trainings](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/): MESA Trainings — short, single-task tutorials for the MESA Portal at mesa.cyverse.org and its apps, written for training participants and for anyone using MESA. Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/index.md
- [Bring your own data to MESA](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/bring-your-own-data/): What data you can bring into MESA to work on, what to leave out, how to get it into your Data Store, how to check it arrived, and what to do if it is not ready. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/bring-your-own-data/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/bring-your-own-data.md
- [MESA website](https://idss-mesa.github.io/): External resource.
- [Documentation](https://idss-mesa.github.io/docs/): External resource.
- [Portal](https://mesa.cyverse.org): External resource.

## Pathways

- [New to MESA](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathways/new-to-mesa/): Sign in, start a notebook, and keep what you make: 3 tutorials to start with, 15 to 25 minutes in all, and more for when you have time. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathways/new-to-mesa/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/pathways/new-to-mesa.md
- [Get ready for a hands-on session](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathways/get-ready-for-a-session/): Arrive signed in, with an app that starts and the practice data loaded: 4 tutorials to start with, 20 to 25 minutes in all, and more for when you have time. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathways/get-ready-for-a-session/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/pathways/get-ready-for-a-session.md
- [Check a dataset before you trust it](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathways/check-a-dataset/): Find out what a dataset holds and where it is incomplete or doubtful: 5 tutorials to start with, 25 minutes in all, and more for when you have time. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathways/check-a-dataset/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/pathways/check-a-dataset.md
- [Work in R](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathways/work-in-r/): Load the practice data in MESA RStudio Geospatial and check its flags: 2 tutorials to start with, 10 to 15 minutes in all, and more for when you have time. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathways/work-in-r/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/pathways/work-in-r.md
- [Use an AI agent and check what it says](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathways/use-an-ai-agent/): Test what an AI assistant tells you against the data, then start an agent of your own: 3 tutorials to start with, 20 minutes in all, and more for when you have time. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathways/use-an-ai-agent/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/pathways/use-an-ai-agent.md
- [Leave work others can rerun](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathways/leave-work-others-can-rerun/): Describe your work and leave a notebook that someone else can run again: 2 tutorials to start with, 15 to 20 minutes in all, and more for when you have time. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathways/leave-work-others-can-rerun/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/pathways/leave-work-others-can-rerun.md
- [Every tutorial, by pathway point](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathway/): Every MESA tutorial under the five points of the learning pathway, from finding your way around to sharing work others can rerun, with the time each takes. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathway/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/pathway.md
- [Self-checks](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathways/self-checks/): Short questions for checking yourself after a tutorial, each with its answer, the likely slips, and how the answer is confirmed against the practice data. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathways/self-checks/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/pathways/self-checks.md
- [Your progress](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/progress/): Where you are on each learning pathway, kept only in your own browser, with ways to save a copy to a file, bring one back, and clear it. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/progress/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/progress.md

## Tutorials

- [Sign in to the MESA Portal with a CyVerse account](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/sign-in/): Sign in to the MESA Portal at mesa.cyverse.org with a free CyVerse account and confirm that you reached your dashboard. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/sign-in/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/sign-in.md
- [Find MESA's community data in the Data Browser](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/find-community-data/): Open the MESA community folder in the portal's Data Browser, confirm where you are from the folder header, and copy a folder's path. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/find-community-data/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/find-community-data.md
- [Ask CyVerse for access to interactive apps](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/request-app-access/): Send the one-time request that lets a new CyVerse account start MESA JupyterLab and the other interactive apps, and know when it has been granted. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/request-app-access/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/request-app-access.md
- [Launch MESA JupyterLab with your Data Store mounted](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/launch-jupyterlab/): Start the MESA JupyterLab app from the MESA Portal and confirm that your CyVerse Data Store is available inside it. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/launch-jupyterlab/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/launch-jupyterlab.md
- [Save your work where it survives the session](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/save-your-work/): Save a notebook inside your Data Store from MESA JupyterLab and confirm from the MESA Portal that it will outlive the app. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/save-your-work/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/save-your-work.md

- [Practice data: five invented rain gauges](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/practice-data/): The synthetic rain-gauge practice dataset used by the data tutorials: what its five files contain, its data dictionary, and how to copy it into your Data Store. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/practice-data/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/practice-data.md
- [Load a file from your Data Store into a notebook](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/load-a-file/): Read a CSV file that sits in your Data Store into a pandas table in MESA JupyterLab and confirm its size against what you expected. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/load-a-file/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/load-a-file.md
- [Read the data dictionary before the data](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/read-the-data-dictionary/): Use a dataset's data dictionary to find out what each column means and which column you cannot yet add up, before you compute anything. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/read-the-data-dictionary/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/read-the-data-dictionary.md
- [Check a column's range and missing values](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/check-range-and-missing/): Find the smallest and largest value in a column and count the blanks in every column, so that an impossible value or a gap shows up before you compute with it. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/check-range-and-missing/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/check-range-and-missing.md
- [Tally a quality flag before you trust a number](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/tally-a-quality-flag/): Count how many rows carry each value of a quality flag, including the blanks, and look at the flagged rows before deciding what to do with them. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/tally-a-quality-flag/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/tally-a-quality-flag.md
- [Count records per day to find incomplete days](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/count-records-per-day/): Count the rows for each gauge and day to find days that were recorded twice and days that were not recorded at all. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/count-records-per-day/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/count-records-per-day.md
- [Reconcile row counts before and after a join](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/reconcile-a-join/): Join a table of readings to a table of gauges and confirm that the join neither added nor lost rows and left no reading without a match. - [Keep tokens and passwords out of saved files](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/keep-secrets-out-of-files/): Give a notebook a token without typing it into a cell, and confirm that the saved notebook does not contain it. ## Explainers

- [What an agent is, and is not](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/explainers/what-an-agent-is/): An agent is a language model that calls tools in a loop and chooses its own next step; this page sets it beside a chat model and a fixed pipeline. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/explainers/what-an-agent-is/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/explainers/what-an-agent-is.md
- [Recalled or retrieved](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/explainers/recalled-or-retrieved/): A figure in an AI agent's answer either came back from a tool call or came from the model's memory, and only the first can be checked against your data. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/explainers/recalled-or-retrieved/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/explainers/recalled-or-retrieved.md
- [Reading what an agent did](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/explainers/reading-what-an-agent-did/): The record of an AI agent's calls can be read like a lab notebook, and it goes wrong in five recognisable ways, each with a tell. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/explainers/reading-what-an-agent-did/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/explainers/reading-what-an-agent-did.md

## Meta

- [Full corpus in one file](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/llms-full.txt): every page's Markdown with frontmatter, links made absolute; about 496 KB, roughly 127,000 tokens. Prefer it over fetching pages one at a time.
- [Update log](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/log/): dated history of changes to this bundle.
- [For AI agents](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/about/ai-agents/): endpoints, trust signals, and what to do if you cannot fetch this site.
- [Sitemap](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/sitemap.xml) and [robots.txt](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/robots.txt): crawlers honour only the origin https://idss-mesa.github.io/robots.txt, which is equally permissive.
- [MESA project site](https://idss-mesa.github.io/llms.txt): origin-level llms.txt indexing the MESA site, the MESA documentation, and the MESA software repositories.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/idss-mesa/trainings): the bundle itself; `docs/` mirrors the site paths one to one.

These pages teach people to use the MESA Portal by hand. For how a feature works, read the MESA documentation at https://idss-mesa.github.io/docs/llms.txt; for CyVerse data itself, connect to the MESA MCP servers and call their tools.
